# Conductor

> Compile and run graphs of typed Python functions.

A node is a function whose typed signature is its interface. A graph binds each node's inputs to other nodes' outputs or typed-in values. Compile gives an immutable `CompiledGraph` that reports what is wrong; the engine runs it as a stream of events, once per row wherever a series arrives. The host declares its own types and nodes.

## Quick Start

One node takes a single value, the other a whole series; that is all iteration is.

```python
from conductor import OPEN, CompiledGraph, From, Graph, NodeRegistry, Series, node


@node("upper")
def upper(text: str) -> str:
    return text.upper()


@node("join")
def join(texts: Series[str]) -> str:
    """Joins every text of a series."""
    return "+".join(texts)


assert upper("a") == "A"  # a node is called like its function

graph = Graph(nodes=[
    upper.graph_node("upper", text=OPEN),
    join.graph_node("join", texts=From("upper.result")),
])
compiled = CompiledGraph.from_graph(graph, NodeRegistry([upper, join]))
ready = compiled.with_inputs(text=["a", "b", "c"])     # by name; by address, **{"upper.text": ...}
assert ready.is_runnable, ready.problems

state = await ready.run()          # in a script: ready.run_sync()
ready.outputs(state)               # {"join.result": "A+B+C"}: what the graph returns, by address
results = ready.results(state)     # every node's outputs, by node id
results["upper"]["result"]         # {"rows": [(0,), (1,), (2,)], "values": ["A", "B", "C"]}: ran once per value
results["join"]["result"]          # "A+B+C": Series[str] received the whole series once
```

`node.graph_node(id, ...)` is a `GraphNode` at the current version, its arguments checked like the function's. A value is typed in; `From(...)` is an edge, and types as `Any`. `OPEN` leaves an input with nothing on it, for the caller or a `FromRun`, and the placed node has no binding for it.

## Core Concepts

### The Node Contract

`@node("id", title=, description=, category=, tags=, docs=, policy=, deprecation=, compute_added_inputs=, compute_outputs=, replaces=, upgrade=)` wraps a plain function and returns a frozen, callable `NodeDefinition`; it registers nothing. Only the id is required: the title defaults to the function's name, the description to its docstring.

- Input: `text: str`, or `Annotated[str, Param(title=, description=, widget=, connectable=)]` beside it. Without a widget an editor shows no control for it: an edge fills it, or a value set in code. A default makes it optional. A type no edge can carry (`list[X]`, a `Literal`) closes the input by itself; `connectable=False` closes one that could.
- Output: `-> str` is one output named `result`, `Result(name=, title=, description=, exclusive_group=)` beside it says more; a frozen dataclass is one output per field; `-> Mapping[str, Any]` returns the computed outputs by name and needs `compute_outputs`; `-> None` declares no outputs.
- `Any` is a value routed unread; an `Any` output needs `compute_outputs` to type it.
- A value can be blank. If an input's type doesn't say `| None` (`email: str | None`), the node isn't called for that row: its outputs are blank there, an `exclusive_group` output is skipped, and an output that makes rows has none. `Series[X]` leaves blanks out, row by row across the series inputs on one index; `Series[X | None]` keeps them. Inputs of many values reading one index stay on the same rows: a row one of them has skipped is blank there, so a zip never pairs two rows, and `Series[X]` then drops that row from all of them. `Any`, `Series[Any]` and `AsItArrives` take blanks. `| None` on a return lets the node return `None`, and a question may be left blank. A default is for an input nothing is wired to, never for a blank. `node_complete.rows_not_called` and `RunState.rows_not_called` count, per input, the rows skipped this way.
- `**x: T` makes every edge an input declared `T` when no `compute_added_inputs` owns the parameter: `Any` or a type runs the node per row, `Series[Any]` reduces each edge, `AsItArrives` hands each as it arrives (a column as a column) and never runs per row.
- The function returns `SKIPPED` on a branch not taken and `AskPerson` when a person must answer (`-> ... | AskPerson`).
- What the run supplies arrives through `FromRun[T]` parameters.
- `@node` checks the function: a bare widget in `Annotated`, an extra conductor does not read, `async def`, an `Any` or `Mapping` return with no hook, and a field name gone from the next version with no `Upgrade` raise `NodeDeclarationError`.

### Versions and Policies

A node's older versions are listed oldest first; the decorated function is the newest. A version's number is its place.

```python
def greet_v1(name: Annotated[str, Param(title="Name", widget=Textarea())]) -> str: ...

def _split_name(values: dict) -> dict:
    first, _, last = values.pop("name").partition(" ")
    return {**values, "first": first, "last": last}

@node("greet", policy=Policy(retries=2, retry_delay=0.5, attempt_timeout=10, concurrency=4), replaces=greet_v1, upgrade=Upgrade(rewrite=_split_name))
def greet(first: str, last: str) -> str: ...
```

- `Policy(retries=0, retry_delay=1.0, attempt_timeout=None, concurrency=8, retry_on=(), reuse_when_inputs_match=True)`; `concurrency` bounds rows in flight, each in a worker thread.
- `replaces=` names the `@node` of the same id this version follows; a version's number is its place in that chain, each version keeps its own policy, hooks and `deprecation=`, and only the newest goes in a registry. `Upgrade(renamed_inputs={old: new}, renamed_outputs={old: new}, rewrite=fn)` goes beside `replaces=`; renames carry lock and content; it is required only when a field name of the replaced version is gone.
- `upgrade_node(graph, node_id, registry, to=None)` moves one node to a version and rewrites edges on renamed outputs, returning a `Graph`; what it can't do is `InvalidCallError`. Compile never upgrades.
- `Deprecation(header=, description=, alternative=, migration=)` retires one version (`deprecation=` on its `@node`); the newest version's notice is the node's; `NodeRegistry` checks an `alternative` exists.
- `NodeDefinition.from_compiled_graphs(id, versions={3: compiled}, title=, description=, category=)` makes a node whose versions are graphs: a host compiles each stored graph version once. The title defaults to the id. Outside it, its fields go by the names it offers: bare where unique, the address on a clash (`text`, `t.text`). Bindings and `From` use them, and inner addresses only read a run. Compile walks the graph node as one node with the graph's `interface`, then puts the graph's nodes in its place under the graph node's id (`approve/check`), under the row the graph node runs on; the run reads exactly as if they had been drawn there. Only the inputs and outputs the graph offers are reachable from outside: an edge or value on any other inner field is `unknown_ref_output` or `stale_binding`. An offered input needs a type: one typed `Any` or `Series[Any]` leaves its node not ready. A graph with anything fatal in it but an input it offers left empty is refused where it is embedded with one fatal `embedded_graph_broken` (`graph`, `problems` in its details); it stays one node with nothing inside, and its own problems stay on it, `compiled.node(id).version.problems`. A value typed on an embedded graph's input, or an edge into an input its author filled, lands on the inner field as if typed or connected there; a value typed there that a hook inside refuses is the hook's own problem on that field of the graph node. Refusing a graph that embeds itself is the host's job.

### Field Hooks

```python
def operand_inputs(count: int) -> list[Input]:                  # what to ADD to the declared inputs
    return [Input(f"value_{i}", float) for i in range(count)]


def branch_outputs(names: str, value: ArrivingType) -> list[Output]:  # all the outputs
    return [Output(name, value, exclusive_group="branches") for name in names.split(",")]
```

Each is a plain function, given per version (`compute_added_inputs=` and `compute_outputs=` on `@node`). A parameter names an input and receives its typed value, the declared default included; a parameter marked `ArrivingType` receives the type one call gets there (the edge's, or the typed-in value's with no edge; `Any` until something is), and `**x: ArrivingType` receives all connected ones. If a value parameter has neither a typed-in value nor a default the hook is not called and the node keeps what it declares. A hook adds inputs only onto a `**x` parameter, and builds records the way a signature reads: `Input("amount", float, widget=...)`, `Output(name, value, exclusive_group="branches")`. A plain Python type closes an `Input`. Compile keeps the answer on `compiled.node(node_id).interface`. `ComputeHookError(message, code=None, ctx=None, field=None)`, the one shape every author error has, becomes a `Problem` on the node.

### Types

`str`, `int`, `float`, `bool`, `date`, `datetime` and a pydantic model travel on edges as they are; compile reads each as a `DType`, so nothing past it knows the difference. `class Text(DType, str)` with an `id`, `display_title` defaulting to the class name, is for a type of your own: one that restricts its edges, a word for a palette, one that formats itself; a subtype lands on its parent, so a `Text` lands on `str`. It never converts or picks a widget. `Input.dtype` and `Output.dtype` are always a `DType`: `Any` is held as a private type whose `id` is `any`, a type no edge can carry as one whose `id` is `setting`. `Series[X]` reads as `Sequence[X]` to a type checker, so a node returns a list; `Table[...]` takes a `TypedDict` naming the columns, and `table_with_columns({"name": Text})` is the same type for a hook.

- `target.accepts(source)`: may an edge land, asked about one value of each side (default `issubclass`). `as_text` formats, `describe()` is its record.
- `registry.types`: node types plus `NodeRegistry(..., types=[...])`; `registry.accepted_as(T)`: ids `T` lands on.
- `Series[X]`: many values of one type, never nested. A word on a signature, not a value: a type checker reads `Sequence[X]`, a node receives a plain list and returns any sequence, and `Input`/`Output` hold `X` in `dtype` with `many=True`. `list[X]` stays one value that is a list. A row is a path, `(i,)` or `(i, j)`.
- `Ref("node.field")` addresses one field.

### Bindings

`Graph(nodes=[...])`; `GraphNode(id=, type=, version=, bindings=, locked=, title=, description=, fields=, display=)`. Each input holds at most one binding; there is no edge record. A node id may not contain `.`, `/` or `@`.

- `From("a.result", ...)`: over edges. Refs on different indexes into a `Series[X]` input gather, each source cut at the node's row as far as the two share one and read whole when they share none; refs on one index are a union, and a row covered twice fails with `row_covered_twice`.
- `Static(...)`: typed in. A list on a scalar input runs the node once per value, under each row the node otherwise runs on: questions set on a node that runs per document run once per question per document. The list is a column too: `node.input` reads from an edge like an output, so answers can sit beside their questions. Only one list may be set on a node (`lists_on_a_per_row_node`).
- No binding: the default. `locked` names inputs no caller may fill. `graph.with_values({"mail.greeting": "hello"})` types a value in on any input an edge doesn't feed, for an author; `with_inputs` fills only what a graph offers its caller.
- `dependencies_of(nodes)`: who waits for whom; an empty set is an input node.

### Compilation

`CompiledGraph.from_graph(graph, registry)` is pure and never raises for a fault in the graph: each is a `Problem` (`type`, `loc`, `msg`, `ctx`, and `fatal`, read off the code). A hook that raises anything but `ComputeHookError` is a bug in the hook and leaves `from_graph` as it is. A required input with a type and nothing bound is a fatal `unbound_required`, but its node stays `ready`: compile types it from its declaration, so the node and everything after it are worked out. Definitions loaded at run time go in `registry.extended_with([cls])`.

- Graph: `problems`, `is_runnable`, `interface` (open inputs, unread outputs), `graph`, `execution_order`, `decisions`. An address is `node.field`; `interface` and `outputs` name an embedded graph's fields the same way, by what it offers (`emb.amount`). Reading a run, `results` uses the path (`Ref("emb/check", "amount")`), and `compiled.field` takes either address.
- `compiled.node(node_id)` answers for every node compile met: `id`, `graph_node`, `embedded_in`, `problems`, `state` (`ready`, `wiring_failed`, `resolution_failed`), `cause` (the one `Problem` behind a node that isn't `ready`), `definition`, `version`, `interface`, `statics`, `embedded_graph` and `fingerprint`. What compile doesn't know is `None`, never an error: `interface` when it can't tell the node's fields, `fingerprint` on a node that doesn't run as one unit. `compiled.field(ref)` hands back one record per field (`ref`, `type`, `binding`, `condition`, `problems`); a node that isn't `ready` or an unknown field is a `KeyError`.
- `compiled.describe()` is what an editor reads to draw the graph, one JSON-ready `GraphDescription`: `is_runnable`, `problems`, `interface`, `run_plan`, `nodes` and `fields`. `nodes` has one `CompiledNodeDescription` per node the author drew (`state`, `interface`, `takes_graph_inputs`), and `fields` has one `FieldDescription` (`dtype`, and `many`, whether it holds many values) per input and output of a `ready` node, by the address an edge writes (`emb.amount` on a node that is a graph), each of which `compiled.field` accepts. An `InterfaceDescription` has `inputs`, `outputs` and `needs`, the names of the `FromRun` types a run must be given. `registry.describe()` is its twin for what can be placed.
- `compiled.run_plan` says where every ready node runs and what each of its inputs receives: `.nodes[node_id]` has `runs_per_row_of` (a `Ref` or `None`), `inputs` (a `ReceiveMode` per input, the record the run reads) and `makes_rows`. Every `ReceiveMode` has `receive_mode` (`value_at_row`, `same_value_every_row`, `all_rows_under_row`, `entire_value`, `collected`, `merged`) and `kind`, which says what else it holds: `cell` has `sources`, `rows_of`, `depth`; `rows_under` has `sources`, `rows_of`, `grouped_under`, `depth`; `fixed` is a static or a default (its value isn't written); `gather` has `source_reads`, one `cell` or `rows_under` per source saying how that source is read at the call's row, and `collected_onto`; `merge` has `source_reads` (a table is a `cell`, a column `rows_under`) and `copied_down`, a table wired in alone being a `cell`. `print(compiled.run_plan)` is the same as text. It is what a host compares between two versions of a graph.
- A field's `condition` says when it has a value: a set of alternatives, each a set of `BranchTaken`, or `ALWAYS` or `NEVER`.

### Rows

A unit is a node on a row; it starts once what it reads exists.

- A series on a single-value input runs the node per row; its outputs are columns on those rows.
- A list returned on a `Series[X]` output makes rows of that output's own (`split.lines`), under the row the node ran on. Two series outputs of one node are two sets of rows, each with its own length; a node fed both per row is `misaligned`.
- A `Series[X]` input receives every value under the node's row, flat, however many levels down. It chooses the node's row only when nothing else does; then the node runs once per row of the level right above the series.
- `SKIPPED` at a row leaves a gap in the column; above the rows it skips the node.

Every level is a table.

- `Table[R]`, whose columns a `TypedDict` names, or bare `Table`, is a whole table in a signature; at run time and to a type checker it is a `polars.DataFrame`. A node takes one and returns one, and it never runs per row because of a `Table` input. Bare `Table` has columns known only when it arrives.
- `| None` on a column changes nothing, a column holds blanks anyway. A column's Polars type is read off what its type is built on (`str`, `float`, `int`, `bool`, `datetime.date`); a type sets `polars_column_type = "Boolean"` only where that base is wrong.
- Every stored table carries a `__row` column (`ROW_ID_COLUMN`), each row's id (`contacts:0`). A returned row with no id, or with one an earlier row holds, gets a fresh one; the others keep theirs. No node declares anything about rows.
- Each column of a `Table[...]` output is a field of its own at `node.output.column` (`csv.result.email`). Wired into a single-value input it runs the node once per row of the table; wired into a `Series[X]` input it gives every row under the node's row. The table is stored once and its cells are read where they sit.
- A blank cell is `None`, and a node running per row isn't called there unless its input says `| None`.
- Several tables or columns wired into one `Table` input are merged on `__row` as the graph runs. A source with another wired source's rows under it is only copied down, so the rows are those of the deepest source and a parent with nothing under it has no row in that table. Sources on the same level keep all their rows, with blanks where one has nothing. A child table a branch skipped gives no rows; a `Table` input fed only skipped sources skips its node.
- A source whose rows can't share an origin with the others (two CSVs read separately) is the fatal `no_rows_in_common` at compile: join them on a key in a node. Tables that are alternatives (one `exclusive_group`, or what hangs off two branches of a decision on a node that runs once) aren't merged: the input receives the branch that ran.
- A table a node rebuilt without `__row` and that is merged with a table it came from fails the node with `row_ids_lost`. Keep the column, or use the table alone.
- A merged column keeps its table column's name, or for a column on its own its output's name; `Result(title=)` names nothing. A column a table carries on from a table it was made from is one column, read from the most derived source that has the row. A real clash takes its output's name (`name_contacts`, `result_2`), the same at compile and at run. A `Table` input's `ArrivingType` is that merged table's type, or what the input declares when it names columns; a frame typed in, the columns it holds.
- A `Table` value is read from a list of records, a Polars frame or the JSON form. `[]` is a table of no rows. A value a column's Polars type can't read goes through its `DType`'s own parsing (a Danish `1,5`). A missing column is `table_column_missing`, naming it in `ctx["column"]`, on a typed-in value and at a call alike.

### Legs and Asking

One call of `compiled.run` is one leg. A run is its `RunState`: every leg returns one, and `status` says how it ended (`complete`, `waiting`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `timed_out`). A node returns `AskPerson(prompt=None, defaults={}, widgets={})`: what is asked is its declared outputs. It and its readers wait, and the leg ends `waiting` with one unit per waiting call in `state.waiting` (`id`, `node_id`, `row`, `prompt`, `questions`). Answering is an edit of the state, and the next leg runs from it:

```python
paused = compiled.run_sync()                                    # paused.status == "waiting"
answers = {asked.id: {"result": "Approved"} for asked in paused.waiting}
answered = compiled.answer(paused, answers)                     # raises here if wrong; no node runs
state = compiled.run_sync(answered)
```

- Each entry of `state.waiting` holds its `prompt` (from `AskPerson(prompt=...)`), the `inputs` it received by name so a form can show the row, many values as a list and a table as its JSON form, exactly what the call got and no more, and the questions it asks.
- Answers are `{waiting.id: {output: value}}`, for a node that ran once, each row, an embedded node or a `Table` output; `None` for a unit means no value on its row. A question left blank takes its default; an `exclusive_group` output left out is the branch not taken. A unit not answered goes on waiting, and a node that asked is not called again unless it or something above it changed.
- A question has `name`, `title`, `description`, `dtype`, `json_schema`, `widget`, `default`, `optional`, `exclusive_group`: enough for a form with no graph loaded.
- A state is plain JSON: `RunState.model_validate_json(saved)`. On the next leg every value passes its output's check, a value that doesn't read fails with `state_unreadable`, and a node whose fingerprint differs runs again with what reads it, reusing a row's earlier result where what it receives is the same (see "Running again"). `run_start`'s `changed_nodes` lists them. `state.without_nodes(node_id)` forces a rerun.
- A parameter typed `FromRun[T]` receives the value of `T` from `compiled.run(from_run={T: value})`; `Interface.needs` is the set of those types. A missing one is `from_run_missing`, at the call.

### Running again

A leg that goes on from a state reuses what it can. A node nothing changed above is restored whole. A changed node's units run again, except a unit whose inputs match one its earlier units received: it takes that result, its cells are written at its new row, and the node isn't called. Reuse comes only from the state you pass: conductor keeps no cache and looks nothing up across runs.

```python
state = compiled.run_sync()                                    # 5,000 mails
state = compiled.with_inputs(contacts=edited).run_sync(state)  # one row added: one mail
```

- The key is what the unit is about to receive, by content, statics and wired values alike (a `FromRun` value is not part of it), plus the node's type, version, input names and output types. A row's position and its id are not, nor are the ids inside a `Table` or a merged table: insert a row at the top and the rows below keep their work, and a whole-table reader sees the same table. A reused unit that took a table and returned one gets the ids of the rows it received now, by position.
- Identical rows don't share a result: each earlier unit is taken once, in row order, so a third identical row is a new call.
- A person's answer goes further than the inputs: it belongs to the question and to the row it was asked on, that row read whole, every row above it, the row its `__row` came from, and which of how many identical rows it is. An answer or a waiting question moves with its row when the row moves. A row replaced by another (Ida's approval doesn't carry to Bo at the same amount), or an edit to any column of the row, even one the form never showed, asks again and re-runs nothing else. Identical rows answered differently keep their answers k-th to k-th while their count holds, and are all asked again when it changes. A waiting unit's `id` (`node@row#hash12`, `node#hash12` for a node that ran once) binds its row and question the same way, so an answer meant for a row that has since moved or changed is refused.
- A node's id is the node: a renamed node is a new node and runs again, sends included.
- The hole: `__row` is a plain column a node can write. A node that swaps ids between rows or copies ids from another table mispairs those rows in a later merge, and an answer bound to such a row follows the wrong one.
- A leg that stops short keeps the earlier work it hadn't reached (`state.nodes[node_id].earlier_units`), so running again from a failed, cancelled, checkpointed or waiting state reuses as much as one uninterrupted leg would.
- `Policy(reuse_when_inputs_match=False)` is for a node whose result depends on the world, not its inputs (a file read by its path, today's exchange rate): a new leg from a `complete` state calls it again, and no earlier unit stands in for it. A leg going on from a waiting, failed or cancelled state keeps what it read.
- `state.without_nodes("a")` forgets only what it names; a node reading it runs again only if what it receives changes. To run `a` and everything after it again, name them all.
- `node_complete.reused_units` and `state.nodes[node_id].reused_units` (the count for that leg) say how much was reused. `run_start` still speaks in nodes (`reused_nodes`, `changed_nodes`).
- **A state goes back only to the runner it came from.** It holds results and hands them to whoever passes it; what the runner could see (`FromRun` values, the world) is not in the key, as it isn't for a resume today.

### Retries and Timeouts

Retries live on the version's `Policy`, per unit.

- Only `ExternalFailure` retries: raised by the node, or wrapped from a class in `Policy.retry_on` (`external_failed`). Anything else is the code `execution_failed`, run once.
- Attempt `n` waits `retry_delay * 2 ** (n - 1)` and emits `node_retry`.
- `Policy.attempt_timeout` bounds one attempt: the unit fails with the code `timeout`, final; the thread is not interrupted.
- `compiled.run(timeout=60)` ends the leg `timed_out`; setting `compiled.run(cancel=asyncio.Event())` ends it `cancelled`. Leaving `async with compiled.stream() as events:` stops every unit.

### Errors

The classes are exported from `conductor`. What is wrong is always one record, `Problem(type, loc, msg, ctx)`: on `compiled.problems`, on `node_failed` and `state.failure`, and in `InvalidCallError.errors()`. Its `type` is a stable code (see "Problem and error codes"); a node failure's `loc` is `(node_id, *row)`, a compile problem's `(node_id, field)`.

```
NodeDeclarationError    a node or type declared wrong, at import; a TypeError, with code and node_id
ComputeHookError        a hook cannot answer; field= says where
InvalidCallError        a verb was given what it cannot act on, every fault listed
NodeError               code, ctx, node_id
└── ExternalFailure         retried
```

A failed unit ends the leg `failed`, its problem on `state.failure`: nothing more starts, the calls already on a thread are waited for (each as far as its `attempt_timeout`) and kept, so a later leg doesn't repeat them, and then the leg ends; `compiled.results(state)` reads what was done and `compiled.outputs(state)` refuses (`run_not_complete`). A call that can't be acted on raises `InvalidCallError`, whose `errors()` lists a `Problem` for every fault, and nothing changes. Running a graph with fatal compile problems raises it too, listing them. A node returning the wrong type is a failed run with `invalid_output`.

### Events

`async with compiled.stream(state) as events:` yields frozen models from `conductor.events`, the union `Event` on `type`; checks are made at the call. `run_start` is always first and `run_end` always last. `run_end` writes only `status`: `event.state` is for the host to save, each value already went out on its own event, and a host that wants the state on the wire writes `event.state.model_dump_json()`. An event is a record, and it writes itself as JSON: `event.model_dump(mode="json")`, `event.model_dump_json()` and a TypeAdapter of `Event` write each value by its own type, a table whole. `to_jsonable(value)` writes a value the same way, as `to_jsonable(compiled.results(state))`. A float that isn't finite is the text `"NaN"`, `"Infinity"` or `"-Infinity"` wherever it stands: a `float` output reads it back; a value typed `Any` comes back as that text, as it comes back as the JSON form of everything else it held. A value with no JSON form raises.

| Event | Carries |
|---|---|
| `node_start`, `node_skipped` | `node_id` |
| `node_progress` | `node_id`, `done`, `total` (`None` until every row exists); at most four a second per node, and always its last count |
| `node_complete` | `node_id`, `outputs`, `rows_not_called`, `reused_units` |
| `node_retry` | `node_id`, `row`, `attempt`, `retries`, `error`, `delay` |
| `node_failed` | `node_id`, `cause` (a `Problem`) |
| `unit_waiting` | `unit` |
| `run_start` | `reused_nodes`, `changed_nodes`, `waiting` |
| `run_checkpoint` | `state`, with status `running` (only with `checkpoint_every`) |
| `run_end` | `state`, which it does not write; `status` is what `event.model_dump` holds |

`compiled.stream(state, checkpoint_every=5.0)` also yields `RunCheckpoint` at most every 5 seconds, when a unit finishes (`0`: every time one does), so a crash loses only what came after the last one saved. `run` and `answer` take its `state` like any other, `results` reads it, and `outputs` refuses it. A finished unit is not called again and one in flight is: a unit runs at least once, so a node with side effects must allow for that. A stored `running` state can't tell a live leg from a crashed one, so a host holds a lease before it resumes one. Building the state is a pass over every value so far, on the event loop; the state is a copy, so dump it on another thread.

### Saving a Graph

Records are frozen pydantic models. `Graph`, `Problem` and `Policy` round-trip; descriptions and widgets are write-only. A ref is stored as `"node.field"`.

```python
graph.to_path("approval.yaml")          # .json, .yaml or .yml
graph = Graph.from_path("approval.yaml")
graph = Graph.from_yaml(graph.to_yaml())
```

### The Palette

`NodeDefinition.describe()` is a `NodeDescription` (`id`, `title`, `description`, `category`, `tags`, `docs`, `deprecation`, `current_version`, `versions`, each with `inputs`, `outputs`, `policy`, `open_input_type`, the type an edge into an open node becomes, `deprecation`). `registry.describe()` has `nodes` and `types` (each a `TypeDescription`: `id`, `title`, `accepted_as`). Printed objects show constructor form.

## API Reference

Three public modules: `conductor`, `conductor.widgets` and `conductor.events`. Each lists its names in `__all__`; import from nothing else.

### conductor

- Nodes: `node`, `NodeDefinition`, `NodeVersion`, `Upgrade`, `upgrade_node`, `Policy`, `Deprecation`, `NodeDescription`, `VersionDescription`, `Interface`, `ArrivingType`, `FromRun`, `Input`, `Output`, `Param`, `Result`
- Returns: `SKIPPED`, `AskPerson`
- Types: `DType`, `AsItArrives`, `Series`, `Table`, `Ref`, `to_jsonable(value)`, `ROW_ID_COLUMN` (the name of a table's hidden row-id column), `ValuesOnRows`
- Registry: `NodeRegistry(nodes, types=())`, immutable (`in`, `[]`, `len`, iteration, `nodes`, `types`, `accepted_as`, `describe`, `extended_with`), `RegistryDescription`, `TypeDescription`
- Graph: `Graph`, `GraphNode`, `FieldContent`, `Binding`, `From`, `Static`, `dependencies_of`, `CompiledGraph`, `CompiledNode`, `CompiledField`, `NodeState`, `GraphDescription`, `CompiledNodeDescription`, `FieldDescription`, `InterfaceDescription`, `Problem`, `RunPlan`, `NodeRunPlan`, `ReceiveMode`, `Condition`, `BranchTaken`, `ALWAYS`, `NEVER`
- Errors: `NodeDeclarationError`, `ComputeHookError`, `InvalidCallError`, `Problem`, `NodeError`, `ExternalFailure`, `PROBLEM_CODES`
- A run's state: `RunStatus`, `WaitingUnit`, `Question`, `Answers`, `OutputColumn`, `WorkOfNode` (what one node did: `fingerprint`, `finished_units`, `answered_rows`, `outputs`, `waiting`, `rows_not_called`, `reused_units`, `earlier_units`), `EarlierUnit`, `RunState` (`status`, `failure`, `waiting`, `nodes`, `without_nodes(...)`); dumped as JSON it is one document holding each table once, under its `tables` key by digest, and a load holds one frame per digest
- Records (`Graph`, `GraphNode`, …) also have `to_yaml()`, `from_yaml(text)`, `to_path(path)`, `from_path(path)`, plus pydantic's.

### Running

Every verb is on `CompiledGraph`:

- `compiled.run(state=None, /, *, from_run=None, timeout=None, cancel=None)`: one leg, its `RunState`. A pause or failure is a `status`. `run_sync` is `run` under `asyncio.run`.
- `compiled.stream(...)`, the same arguments: an async context manager yielding the events.
- `compiled.answer(state, answers)`: a new state with these units answered; no node runs.
- `compiled.with_inputs(**inputs)`: a copy with inputs filled as `Static`s, by bare name or address; a name it doesn't offer or a value its type can't read raises `InvalidCallError`, every fault at once; `compiled.graph` is then what ran.
- `compiled.results(state)`: every node's outputs so far, by node id, `{"rows": [...], "values": [...]}` (`ValuesOnRows`) for an output holding many (`compiled.field(ref).many`), the rows that have values so far. `compiled.outputs(state)`: narrowed to `compiled.interface.outputs`, by address, on a `complete` state only.

### Problem and error codes

A `Problem`'s `type` comes from one table, each code with its English and whether it is fatal, and a host translates by it, filling its sentence from `ctx`. `PROBLEM_CODES` is every code conductor itself writes, for a test that pins your translations to it. A code that isn't in it is your own, from a hook or a node, and is always fatal.

### conductor.widgets

Frozen models with a `kind`, and a host subclasses `Widget` for a control of its own; compile and the engine never read one. `title`, `description`, `connectable` and the limits of a value (`ge`, `gt`, `le`, `lt`, `min_length`, `max_length`, `pattern`) belong to the `Param`, and a value outside its limits is refused. An untitled field reads as its name in everyday words. No type has a default widget.

| Widget | Options |
|---|---|
| `TextWidget` | none |
| `Textarea` | `rows` |
| `Dropdown` | `choices` (`Choice(id, title)`) |
| `NumberWidget` | `step`, `integer_only` |
| `Range` | `step` |
| `Switch` | none |
| `DatePicker` | `seed` |
| `FileUpload` | `accept`, `max_size_mb`, `multiple` |
| `ListWidget` | none |

### conductor.events

Every event record: `Event` (the union on `type`), `RunStart`, `NodeStart`, `NodeProgress`, `NodeComplete`, `NodeSkipped`, `NodeFailed`, `NodeRetry`, `UnitWaiting`, `RunCheckpoint`, `RunEnd`.

## Workspace Packages

`syv-conductor` (`conductor`), `syv-conductor-nodes` (`conductor_nodes`), `syv-conductor-providers` (`conductor_providers`), released in lockstep; `syv-conductor[all]` installs all three.

### conductor-nodes

Standard nodes declare `str`, `float` and `bool`; `conductor_nodes.types` has `Json` and the decorator `stdlib_node`. `conductor_nodes.registry(*, categories=None)` builds a registry; `conductor_nodes.nodes(*, categories=None)` lists the definitions for a registry of your own.

| Category | Node ids |
|---|---|
| `text` | `text-uppercase`, `text-lowercase`, `text-trim`, `text-length`, `text-concat`, `text-replace`, `text-contains`, `text-split`, `text-join`, `text-reverse` |
| `math` | `math-add`, `math-subtract`, `math-multiply`, `math-divide`, `math-modulo`, `math-round`, `math-min`, `math-max`, `math-abs` |
| `logic` | `logic-not` |
| `control` | `logic-if-empty`, `logic-if-equals`, `decision` (routes a value on a `bool`) |
| `json` | `json-parse`, `json-stringify`, `json-get` |
| `regex` | `regex-match`, `regex-replace`, `regex-extract` (past `.timeout` fails `pattern_timeout`) |

### conductor-providers

- `conductor_providers.mermaid`: `flowchart(compiled)`, a Mermaid flowchart labelling how each edge is received.
- There is no HTTP adapter. `docs/serving-runs.md` is a page of FastAPI routes to copy into your own application: `GET /nodes`, `POST /compile`, and a run you start, follow, read, answer and cancel by id. A leg is an asyncio task on the process that started it, so following and cancelling work only there.

## Project Structure

```
packages/
├── conductor/src/conductor/            __init__, widgets, events: the three public modules
│   ├── about/                          this document
│   └── _internal/                      everything else; import nothing from here
├── conductor-nodes/src/conductor_nodes/
└── conductor-providers/src/conductor_providers/   mermaid/
```

## CLI Reference (this document)

```bash
python -m conductor.about                 # full text
python -m conductor.about sections        # section slugs
python -m conductor.about rows            # one section (prefix or substring)
```

Or `from conductor.about import get_content, list_sections, get_section`.
